title: fleet renders a dirty source_commit as a clean one, so unprovenanced bytes read as provenanced
body:
## Tags

fleet, manifest, provenance, false-signal, documentation

## Summary

`devbin fleet`'s scan rendered the manifest's `source_commit` with `${sc:0:12}`. When a vendor was taken from a dirty seam, `install` writes that field as `<sha> +dirty -- THESE BYTES MATCH NO COMMIT` (`lib/install`, the marker added by issue 0033). Truncating to twelve characters kept the sha and threw away the sentence saying the sha does not describe these bytes.

So `intent/docs/devbin-users.md` -- the one document on this fleet whose entire subject is provenance -- rendered "no commit matches these bytes" as a confident, ordinary-looking commit, in a column indistinguishable from a clean one.

## Reproduction

An install whose manifest carries the dirty form:

```
# source_commit: deadbeefcafe1234 +dirty -- THESE BYTES MATCH NO COMMIT
```

`fleet audit` renders `deadbeefcafe`. `fleet doc` writes `| deadbeefcafe |` into the Source commit column. Nothing anywhere in the output says the bytes are unprovenanced.

## Root Cause

`bin/.devbin/cmd/fleet`, in `scan`: one substring expansion applied to a field that is not always a bare sha. The field's two forms were never distinguished because only the clean form was ever in front of me while writing it -- every estate on the fleet happened to be clean at the moment the command was built and at every run since.

## Impact

The failure is silent and points the wrong way. An estate whose vendored bytes match no commit is exactly the estate a re-vendor decision most needs to see, and this rendered it as the most ordinary row in the table. It also quietly weakens the document's own argument: the doc tells its reader to group by digest "because the stamp records which commit a re-vendor was run from", and one reason those two can disagree is precisely the case the column was hiding.

Not severity-high only because the digest column beside it is unaffected and remains a true statement about the bytes.

## How it was found

Not by a test and not by review. A peer node (utilz/cc) reported an unrelated cosmetic defect in `lib/install`; checking whether that file's change had reached the fleet turned up an estate whose recorded stamp and seam digest could not both be true, and chasing THAT disagreement reached the renderer. The disagreement was the only visible symptom, and it was visible for about one hour before a re-vendor erased it.

## Resolution -- FIXED

`scan` now splits the field before truncating: the sha is shortened to twelve characters and the marker is preserved as a `+dirty` suffix. `UNRECORDED` is untouched. The digest column is unchanged and remains the byte-level answer.

## Verification -- DRIVEN RED FIRST, INCLUDING ONE FALSE GREEN

Two tests in `tests/unit/fleet.bats`, one at the scan boundary and one over the written document.

The document test PASSED on its first run against the unfixed code -- because the fixture project was named `dirtyproj` and the assertion `[[ "$row" == *dirty* ]]` was matching the project's own NAME in the path column. Renamed to `smudged`; both tests then failed for the stated reason, and both pass against the fix.

The document test also carries a positive control: a genuinely clean estate in the same run must NOT gain the marker, so an implementation that flagged everything would fail.

Suite 770 -> 772, rc 0. `check syntax` 32/0, `check lint` 32/0.

## Related

- 0033 -- created the `+dirty` marker this renderer was discarding. The fix landed the marker correctly at the writer and nothing checked that any reader could carry it.
- `usage-rules.md` -- a gate that examines nothing must fail; a column that cannot express "unknown" is the documentation-side form of the same rule.
